name: stream
title: Stream
description: Read from system-in and write to system-out and system-err streams.
label: file,core

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Kind of stream to use such as System.in, System.out, a file, or a http url.

properties.name: encoding
properties.description: You can configure the encoding (is a charset name) to use text-based streams (for example, message body is a String object). If not provided, Camel uses the JVM default Charset.

properties.name: fileName
properties.description: When using the stream:file URI format, this option specifies the filename to stream to/from.

properties.name: fileWatcher
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: To use JVM file watcher to listen for file change events to support re-loading files that may be overwritten, somewhat like tail --retry

properties.name: groupLines
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: To group X number of lines in the consumer. For example to group 10 lines and therefore only spit out an Exchange with 10 lines, instead of 1 Exchange per line.

properties.name: groupStrategy
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Allows to use a custom GroupStrategy to control how to group lines.

properties.name: httpHeaders
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: When using stream:http format, this option specifies optional http headers, such as Accept: application/json. Multiple headers can be separated by comma. The format of headers can be either HEADER=VALUE or HEADER:VALUE. In accordance with the HTTP/1.1 specification, leading and/or trailing whitespace is ignored

properties.name: httpUrl
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: When using stream:http format, this option specifies the http url to stream from.

properties.name: initialPromptDelay
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Initial delay in milliseconds before showing the message prompt. This delay occurs only once. Can be used during system startup to avoid message prompts being written while other logging is done to the system out.

properties.name: promptDelay
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Optional delay in milliseconds before showing the message prompt.

properties.name: promptMessage
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Message prompt to use when reading from stream:in; for example, you could set this to Enter a command:

properties.name: readLine
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Whether to read the input stream in line mode (terminate by line breaks). Setting this to false, will instead read the entire stream until EOL.

properties.name: retry
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Will retry opening the stream if it's overwritten, somewhat like tail --retry If reading from files then you should also enable the fileWatcher option, to make it work reliable.

properties.name: scanStream
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: To be used for continuously reading a stream such as the unix tail command.

properties.name: scanStreamDelay
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Delay in milliseconds between read attempts when using scanStream.

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: appendNewLine
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Whether to append a new line character at end of output.

properties.name: autoCloseCount
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Number of messages to process before closing stream on Producer side. Never close stream by default (only when Producer is stopped). If more messages are sent, the stream is reopened for another autoCloseCount batch.

properties.name: closeOnDone
properties.label: producer
properties.description: This option is used in combination with Splitter and streaming to the same file. The idea is to keep the stream open and only close when the Splitter is done, to improve performance. Mind this requires that you only stream to the same file, and not 2 or more files.

properties.name: delay
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Initial delay in milliseconds before producing the stream.

properties.name: lazyStartProducer
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: readTimeout
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Sets the read timeout to a specified timeout, in milliseconds. A non-zero value specifies the timeout when reading from Input stream when a connection is established to a resource. If the timeout expires before there is data available for read, a java.net.SocketTimeoutException is raised. A timeout of zero is interpreted as an infinite timeout.
